title: Tabbouleh
subtitle: Lebanese herb and bulgur wheat salad
excerpt: A bright, herb-forward Lebanese salad where flat-leaf parsley and mint are the main ingredient, not a garnish. Bulgur wheat, tomato, and spring onion play a supporting role. Dressed generously with lemon and olive oil.
sourceNotes: Tabbouleh is considered Lebanon's national salad and is eaten across the Levant. The Lebanese version uses far more parsley than bulgur, which distinguishes it from other regional interpretations. It appears consistently in cookbooks from the early 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bulgur can be soaked ahead. Dress and add the herbs no more than 30 minutes before serving.

content.text: Chop the parsley very finely. Coarsely chopped parsley gives the salad a rough, undressed feel. Use a sharp knife and go over it twice.
Put the bulgur wheat in a bowl. Pour over 200ml of boiling water and a pinch of salt.
Cover and leave for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Spread the bulgur on a tray and leave to cool completely.
Combine the cooled bulgur, parsley, mint, tomato, spring onion, and cucumber in a large bowl.
Pour over the lemon juice and olive oil.
Taste. Add more lemon juice or olive oil as needed. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Salad is watery at the bottom of the bowl.
items.cause: Tomatoes were not deseeded, or the salad sat too long after dressing.
items.fix: Deseed the tomatoes and serve within 30 minutes of dressing.

items.symptom: Bulgur wheat is chewy and undercooked.
items.cause: Not enough boiling water or insufficient soaking time.
items.fix: Add a little more boiling water and cover for a further 5 minutes.
